channel.description: Recently added myths, legends, ghosts and folklore from across Britain and Ireland.

item.title: Kitty Kilroy, the Witch of Huntsfield
item.description: A priest's horse was said to collapse paralysed on the Huntsfield road, and the villagers who watched dared suggest fetching the local witch to cure it.

item.title: Benlli Gawr, the Tyrant of Foel Fenlli
item.description: A tyrant giant-king of Powys who turned away a wandering saint was consumed, with his entire hillfort, by fire that fell from heaven that same night.

item.title: Betty Wells, the Witch of Kirton in Lindsey
item.description: An elderly neighbour swore for decades that Betty Wells was a 'real witch' — a belief villagers still repeated a century after her supposed heyday.

item.title: Cribarth, the Sleeping Giant
item.description: A mountain silhouette above the Tawe Valley is said to be a giant named Yscydion, lying asleep until Arthur returns and calls him to defend his people.

item.title: Culver Hole and the Smugglers of Port Eynon
item.description: A stone-walled sea cave on the Gower coast was said to be smuggler John Lucas's contraband store, reached by a tunnel wide enough to ride a horse through.

item.title: Feolagan of Kebock Head

item.title: Haltadans, the Petrified Trows of Fetlar
item.description: A stone circle on Fetlar marks the spot where a band of trows danced so wildly to a captured fiddler's tune that dawn caught and turned them all to stone.

item.title: John Olliver, the Miller of Highdown Hill
item.description: A Sussex windmiller built his own tomb 27 years before he died, then reputedly used it to store contraband while signalling smugglers with his sails.

item.title: Lowri and Siân Owen, the Witches of Llanarmon
item.description: Two sisters near Pwllheli ran a cottage "school" where they cast out unclean spirits by ceremony and could read the sea's ebb and flow before it turned.

item.title: Old Mother Digby of East Harting
item.description: A Sussex hare-witch could be caught out only by her own wounds — when a hound tore the hare she had become, the injury turned up on her body at home.

item.title: Saxa and Herman, the Rival Giants of Unst
item.description: Two feuding giants hurled boulders at each other across a Shetland inlet until a mermaid lured both to their deaths in a swimming race to the North Pole.
